metadata.method_name: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ban-landing replication of Claim 1 (frozen bench, 12 tasks)
metadata.description: Ban-free forecasts (SUBTRACT via exact signature vetoes, LADDER via generic pushes incl. matched-norm random directions, ASSOCIATE, PROXIMITY) committed before sampling the bans; scored by the frozen C1 rule.

rule.D: >=10 correct and lead >= 2 -> modal correct label, else modal attempted (D_from_attempts)
rule.present_minor: A != D, >=10% of correct, >=3 correct, task >=10 correct; at most 6 by share
rule.homogeneity: FFH Monte Carlo 100k seed 0; p<0.01 -> decision set = 100 bf16 free samples

deviations.what: One NVIDIA L4 (23 GB, 300 GB/s), 6 CPUs, 57 GB RAM instead of the planned RTX A4500.
deviations.cost: Slower decoding; bf16 still fits (KV cache 41,200 tokens). No change to the model or decoding.

deviations.what: Weights are read from the run's shared HF cache (HF_HUB_CACHE), not a workspace hf_cache/.
deviations.reason: The run's instructions forbid overriding HF_HOME/HF_HUB_CACHE (duplicate blobs).
deviations.cost: None; shard sha256s verified against exp10 (results/model_record.json). No hf_cache/ in the workspace.

deviations.what: RLIMIT_AS is set only for CPU stages (24 GB), not for GPU sessions.
deviations.reason: An address-space cap breaks CUDA/UVM reservations and safetensors mmap (first launch failed with ENOMEM).
deviations.cost: GPU processes rely on the container cgroup limit (57 GB) instead of a catchable MemoryError.

deviations.what: vLLM 0.11 runs with enforce_eager=True and TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1.
deviations.reason: No C compiler in the container (Triton/Inductor cannot build), as in exp10/exp11.

deviations.what: max_num_seqs 32 for B1/B4, then 64 for every later session.
deviations.reason: Decode is weight-bandwidth bound on the L4; 64 concurrent sequences doubled throughput (~350 -> ~600 tok/s).
deviations.cost: None for the sampling distribution (explicit per-request seeds; batch-shape numerics only).

deviations.what: The random-direction pushes (E3) run in vLLM with prefill-only forward hooks on decoder layers 11-21 (same arithmetic as the planned HF hooks: n_{l,i} * r_l added to the residual stream at the spec positions of registered prompts); prefix caching is off in that session. HF is used for the prompt-only ban norms (E1) and the hook tests (T4).
deviations.reason: HF generate on the L4 would have cost ~1 GPU-h (batches run to the longest sample); vLLM keeps every arm in one sampling engine, removing an engine confound.
deviations.cost: None measured: zero-norm hook run identical to the hook-free run 10/10; perturbed-token count exact; added/target norm 0.9998.

deviations.what: T4 'realised layer-21 displacement within 10% of n_21' is met for the per-layer ADDED vector (ratio 1.000), not for the cumulative stream displacement, which is ~3x n_21 because pushes at layers 11-20 propagate.
deviations.reason: Matched norms are applied per layer, as frozen.
deviations.cost: The random pushes displace layer 21 more than the ban does (reported in results/tests_hooks_hf.json); LADDER inputs are therefore generous pushes.

deviations.what: Generated token ids are stored inline in data/raw_gen.jsonl (out_ids), not data/gen_ids/*.npz.
The 12 frozen tasks have 50 modes (54 includes the excluded R2), so B2 = B3 round 1 = 1,000 requests.
Transient HTTP 429 from the j1 judge provider; failed calls were retried by the next combine pass (cache keyed by code sha), never counted as labels.
deviations.cost: None (no unresolved label kept unless reported).

deviations.what: 'Correctly labelled Llama forced programs' = forced programs labelled as requested (adherent), any pass status; a survivor with none uses its bench reference (flagged in predictions/proximity.json).
deviations.reason: Llama passes few tests on several modes; adherence is the labelling notion of 'correctly labelled'.

deviations.what: The frozen scoring rule (src/scoring.py) and forecast code (src/forecasts.py) were copied into predictions/ and hash-chained before the first ban sample; src/analysis.py (descriptive layers, sensitivities, tables) was completed after the commit.
deviations.cost: Descriptive layers were not pre-registered as code; the C1 rule and every forecast were.

deviations.what: 'No family's top-1 hits the landing more often than chance' is tested with a one-sided exact binomial test at 0.05 against the mean chance rate 1/|S| over gated events; if no family advances but some family is above chance the branch is 'NO FAMILY ADVANCES (aimed, unresolved)'.
deviations.reason: The plan names the branch, not the test.

deviations.what: T2: identical-seed reruns reproduce 16/20 samples exactly (prefix-cache/batch numerics); T=1.0 vs a deliberate T=0.6 run at the same seeds are identical in 3/20 (defaults do not leak).

Veto continuations were first decoded with HF's default clean_up_tokenization_spaces=True, which rewrites spacing such as ' ,' -> ',' (594 of 3,104 hit rows; extracted code changed in 590). Before the commit, every hit row was re-decoded exactly (clean_up_tokenization_spaces=False, identical to vLLM's own detokenisation: 0/600 mismatches on B4) and the 590 programs were re-labelled (results/veto_decode_fix.json).
deviations.reason: Bug found by the T3 post-hoc decode check.
deviations.cost: The iterated-round decisions (which rounds ran, which n-grams were added) were taken on the first labels; the committed forecasts use the corrected labels.

deviations.what: Screen prompts use exp10's own builders verbatim (src/config.py copied to screen10/config.py with its workspace import patched; neutral twins padded with ' -'); exp10's canonical labeller runs from a writable copy (screen10/canon) whose judge is exp10's (openai/gpt-4.1-mini).
deviations.reason: Comparability with exp10's landings, which were labelled by that labeller.
deviations.cost: Two labellers in one artifact (bench and canon); never pooled.

drops.reason: Drop order item 1 (time budget on the L4).

drops.what: The path-task screen ran B6 (vetofree pass-1, nonce, novelty), D4 (one-shot, persistent and iterated vetoes) and H6 scoring, but no random-direction pushes on T1/T2: the screen's LADDER pools the nonce ban and the novelty instruction only.
drops.reason: Drop order (random directions are cut before the vetoes); the screen was added after the bench pipeline finished.
drops.cost: The screen LADDER has fewer generic pushes than the bench LADDER.

drops.reason: Descriptive only in iteration 3; no Llama bench FRLP sets exist.

drops.what: T2's HF top_k=0 assertion is moot: no HF sampling is done (HF only runs forward passes).

Task: write a Python function solve(nums, k) that returns the k-th smallest value in nums. The argument nums is a list of integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and every value lies between -10000 and 10000 inclusive; values may repeat. The argument k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(nums), counted from 1, so k = 1 asks for the minimum and k = len(nums) for the maximum. Repeated values are counted separately: for nums = [3, 1, 3] and k = 3 the answer is 3.
